Title: Members of public, NGOs await Tuanku Muhriz's returns
Article:
SEPANG: The situation outside the VVIP Room at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 remained calm and under control tonight as members of the public and representatives of several non-governmental organisations (NGOs) gathered ahead of the arrival of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Tuanku Muhriz is expected to arrive at 9.50pm.
Those gathered were seen waiting at the terminal to welcome Tuanku Muhriz and express their support for the ruler.
Sekretariat Taat Setia Sokongan Yang Dipertuan Besar Negri Sembilan chairman Datuk Seri Megat D Shahriman Zaharudin said the gathering was intended to be peaceful and focused on expressing support and loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz and the royal institution.
He said the members of the public and NGOs had gathered amid the ongoing political situation in Negri Sembilan.
Earlier, according to a poster circulating on social media, members of the public and NGOs were urged to gather at the terminal to welcome and show their support for the ruler.
The gathering is said to be organised by Profans, Waris Dato Siamang Gagap, Waris Negri Sembilan and Pekan.
Tuanku Muhriz's return comes amid conflicting positions over a proclamation concerning his removal as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-GC: Negri Sembilan govt has no power to unilaterally remove Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Negri Sembilan menteri besar and state executive council do not have the unilateral power to terminate or vacate the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) said.
In a statement responding to the Negri Sembilan government's announcement on the position of the state ruler, the A-GC said the validity and legal effect of the April 19 proclamation must be determined through the constitutional and legal process under the Negri Sembilan Constitution.
The A-GC said the proclamation was invalid as it did not comply with the mandatory requirements of Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan Constitution, particularly as there was no evidence that any of the disqualifying grounds under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir

Title: Selangor allocates up to RM20mil to resolve strata title ownership issue
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government has allocated up to RM20 million over two years from 2025 to resolve outstanding issues involving strata title ownership in the state.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the resolution process involved more than building plan approvals, local authority matters, land office procedures and land tax payments, as it also required the collection and updating of property owners' information.
"Imagine a single strata development with more than 200 units, sometimes thousands, where the process of entering data and information can take a long time.
"We require a more comprehensive process because several steps that were overlooked in the past need to be addressed," he said when launching the presentation ceremony for the 2026 Selangor Strata Community Empowerment Initiative today.
Meanwhile, State Housing and Culture Committee chairman Datuk Borhan Aman Shah said the state government, through the Selangor Housing and Property Board (LPHS), had allocated RM5.68 million for three strata community empowerment initiatives in 2026.
He said the initiatives comprised the CERIA Scheme, the Apartment Revitalisation and Selangor Community Strengthening (SPARK) Programme, and the C-SMART 2.0 Programme.
"Of the total, RM5.16 million is allocated under the CERIA Scheme to carry out repair works at 12 strata housing schemes.
"Meanwhile, RM184,000 is being channelled through the SPARK Programme to 23 apartment complexes, with a grant of RM8,000 per complex, while RM340,000 has been allocated for C-SMART 2.0, involving 12 local authorities across Selangor," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pestec wins fresh injunction against Speco
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pestec International Bhd has secured an ad interim injunction from the Kuala Lumpur High Court against Shandong Power Equipment Co Ltd (Speco).
The interim injunction restrained Speco from enforcing or taking steps to enforce an undated corporate guarantee linked to an ongoing legal dispute.
The order follows an ex parte injunction granted by the court on Sept 2, according to Pestec's bourse filing on Thursday.
Under the latest order, Speco, including its employees, agents and representatives, is restrained from enforcing, executing, demanding or taking any action to enforce the undated corporate guarantee until the inter partes hearing on Oct 9, or until further order of the court.
The parties are also allowed to make any applications they deem necessary before the hearing.
The legal action stems from a civil suit filed by Pestec and its subsidiaries Enersol Co Ltd and Pestec Sdn Bhd at the Kuala Lumpur High Court against, among others, Speco, Shandong Electrical Engineering & Equipment Group Co (SDEE) and certain former members of Pestech's management.
Pestec said it will take further steps to protect its rights and interests regarding a winding-up petition filed by Speco.
The latest court order does not determine the underlying merits of the dispute, with the matter set for an inter partes hearing on Oct 9.
Pestec has been involved in power infrastructure and engineering projects in Malaysia and overseas.
Its business spans transmission and distribution systems, substations and renewable energy-related infrastructure.
Speco and SDEE are Chinese power equipment and engineering companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix founder Wong Thean Soon sheds 103.62mil Cuscapi shares, no longer substantial shareholder
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd's founder Wong Thean Soon is no longer a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi Bhd after disposing of about 103.62 million shares.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Cuscapi said Wong disposed of about 99.12 million shares on Sept 11 while his private vehicle Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd disposed of another 4.5 million shares.
The total shares equaled nearly an 11 per cent stake in Cuscapi.
Based on Cuscapi's closing price of five sen on Sept 11, the shares Wong disposed of totalled about RM5.18 million.
Investor Tan Boon Seng acquired about 103.62 million shares in Cuscapi on the same day Wong disposed of his stakes, representing a 10.6 per cent stake in the company.
Following the recent disposal, Wong currently holds about 23.25 million shares in the company or about a a 2.5 per cent stake.
Cuscapi's share price closed one sen or 20 per cent higher at six sen on Thursday, valuing the company at RM56.69 million.

Title: 20 flights affected by Kota Kinabalu Airport runway closure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The temporary closure of the runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has affected 20 flights today, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said.
In a statement today, MAHB said the runway remained temporarily closed to allow essential works to be completed safely, with continuous rainfall affecting the progress of the works.
"We are working closely with the airlines to manage the operational impact and support affected passengers.
"Safety remains our highest priority, and flight operations will resume only when the runway is confirmed safe for use," it said.
Passengers are advised to check their latest flight status directly with their respective airlines.
MAHB apologised for the inconvenience and thanked passengers for their patience and understanding.

Title: KL to create 49ha of new recreational spaces, boosts protection for green areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will create nearly 49 hectares of new recreational spaces and public parks across the capital, as part of efforts to expand the city's network of green areas and recreational facilities.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the strategic initiative included pre-development works and the utilisation of Department of Irrigation and Drainage reserves along Sungai Bunus and Kolam Ayer Panas.
She said the development will also cover the pond area next to Jalan Tasik Permaisuri 3, as well as a phased project at the Kampung Sungai Bohol Retention Pond.
"Our main aim under this initiative is not merely to create new recreational spaces, but to ensure that every valuable open and green space in Kuala Lumpur is legally gazetted and protected," she said after inspecting the Bunus Flood Retention Pond today.
She said the areas will be equipped with basic infrastructure suitable for people of all ages, particularly senior citizens and children, such as jogging tracks and lighting, while enforcement will be tightened to prevent encroachment or unauthorised commercial activities.
Yeoh said that through the continued efforts of the Federal Territories Land and Mines Office (PPTGWP), 556 open-space lots have now been gazetted, while more than 200 others are in the final stages of the gazettement process.
She said the transparency of the gazettement process allows city residents to check the list of protected open spaces themselves through the MyHijau application on the official PPTGWP portal.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL allocates more than RM200 million under Budget 2027 for the green cluster, covering the management, preservation and upgrading of public facilities.
He said DBKL submitted an application to the Finance Ministry under a matching grant scheme to upgrade 14 neighbourhood children's playgrounds to safer, more modern designs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Early Kelantan polls unnecessary to prove Pas' sincerity, says deputy MB
Article:
KOTA BHARU: Kelantan believes there is no need for the state to hold an early state election merely to prove Pas' sincerity towards Umno.
Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the recent state elections in Johor and Negri Sembilan had already demonstrated the party's sincerity.
"The Kelantan state government is stable. There is no need to hold an early election.
"The two state elections in Johor and Negri Sembilan have demonstrated the success of the cooperation between these two major parties, and that is sufficient proof of Pas's commitment and sincerity," he said when contacted.
At the 2026 Umno General Assembly, deputy president
Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has proposed
that one of the "SG4" states, specifically Terengganu, hold an election to test prospective political partners' sincerity in pursuing cooperation.
He said this would show whether cooperation in the name of Malay-Muslim unity reflected a genuine willingness to share power or merely benefited one side.
SG4, or State Government 4, is a cooperation platform comprising the four Perikatan Nasional-led states of Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KKIA flight operations disrupted by temporary runway closure
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Several flights at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) were delayed, cancelled or diverted this evening following the temporary closure of its runway for rectification works.
Checks by Bernama at about 5.40pm found several arriving flights from Tawau, Johor Baru, Kuala Lumpur and Guangzhou listed as delayed on the airport's flight information display.
At least two arriving flights from Lahad Datu and Labuan were also listed as cancelled on the display at the time.
KKIA Head of Operations Hassim Duman said the runway was initially scheduled to close for two hours from 2.45pm today to facilitate rectification works.
However, a Sabah Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) source said a new Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) was subsequently issued, extending the runway closure from 5pm to 8pm today.
Malaysia Airports, in a statement on its official Facebook page, said the runway would reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works had been completed.
An airline source said several arriving flights had been diverted to Labuan and Sandakan following the runway closure.
Meanwhile, passenger Mohd Rasedi Che Mamat, 67, said his flight to Sandakan, scheduled for 12.20pm after a medical check-up at Queen Elizabeth Hospital II, remained delayed into the evening.
"I am really worried. Sitting for such a long time is very difficult for me, and my backside is really hurting. If the delay continues until tomorrow, I do not know how I will manage to sit here. I will have to discuss it with my daughter first," he told Bernama.
Rasedi said he had travelled to Kota Kinabalu for a heart-related medical check-up and opted to fly back to Sandakan as travelling by road would be difficult given his condition.
Another passenger, Mohd Firman Syah Zainal, 32, who came from Sipitang which is 145km from here, said his flight to Kuala Lumpur, originally scheduled for 6pm, had been delayed to 8.45pm and he was worried it could be further delayed or cancelled.
"I am worried. My hometown is far away. It takes three hours to get there from here. I have to report for work in Kuala Lumpur tomorrow, so I am really worried if the flight is cancelled or delayed until tomorrow," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Superbike rider survives crash after flying into Audi's path [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A superbike rider was thrown into the path of an oncoming Audi after overshooting a corner in Jelebu, Negri Sembilan, in a crash that unfolded within seconds.
A video of the incident circulating on social media showed the rider losing control while taking the bend before being flung across the road and into the Audi's lane.
The Audi driver, identified on social media as Zarul, said the rider suffered a broken rib and was receiving treatment in hospital.
"Alhamdulillah, it could have been much worse," he said, urging motorists and motorcyclists to remain alert and leave enough space to react to unexpected hazards.
"Sometimes it's not even you. You can be minding your own business and suddenly someone else's mistake becomes your situation too. So anticipate, give yourself space and pay attention to everyone around you."
A second rider, believed to have been travelling with him, also lost control after braking hard and losing traction, falling in front of the now-stationary Audi.
The driver said the incident reminded him that road crashes could happen within seconds, even when a road user was simply going about their journey.
"Cars can be repaired. What matters today is that everyone is still here, and sometimes it's not about being right. It's about making it home," he said.
He also thanked those who stopped to assist after the crash.
The footage showed the Audi swerving at the last moment as the superbike rider entered its path.
A check of the comments on the post showed many social media users expressing relief that the rider survived the crash.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Reservoir Link lands RM570mil solar project, signs 30-year PPA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Reservoir Link Energy Bhd has secured a 30-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Syarikat Sesco Bhd for a 200MWac solar photovoltaic project in Tinjar, Sarawak, with an estimated development cost of RM570 million.
Sesco is a wholly-owned subsidiary of state-owned Sarawak Energy Bhd.
The project, spanning about 243.8 hectares, will be Reservoir Link's largest single renewable energy project, the company said in a bourse filing today.
Construction is targeted to begin in January 2028, with commercial operations scheduled for Dec 31, 2029.
Once operational, the solar plant is expected to export about 401GWh of electricity to the Sarawak grid annually, enough to power an estimated 100,000 households.
Reservoir Link's indirect wholly-owned subsidiary RL Kenyalang Solar Sdn Bhd, signed the agreement and will build, own, operate and maintain the facility.
Under the PPA, RL Kenyalang will generate and deliver solar energy to Sesco, which will purchase the project's net electrical output at the prescribed energy rate.
Sesco will make monthly payments for the delivered electricity.
The PPA will remain in force for 30 years from the commercial operation date, unless extended or terminated earlier in accordance with its terms.
Reservoir Link said the project is not expected to materially impact its earnings or net assets per share for the financial year ending June 30, 2027.
The impact on gearing will depend on the final financing arrangements, which are yet to be determined.
Reservoir Link slipped into the red in FY26, posting a net loss of RM68.12 million compared with a net profit of RM29.47 million a year earlier.
Revenue fell 37.7 per cent to RM78.14 million from RM125.40 million.
Its shares closed unchanged at 31.5 sen today, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM122.9 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six Myanmar nationals held in RM1.2mil Lipis illegal mining raid
Article:
LIPIS: An illegal iron ore mining site raided yesterday led to the arrest of six undocumented Myanmar nationals and the seizure of machinery and vehicles worth about RM1.2 million.
The men, aged between 22 and 39, had been working at the Sungai Lik, Cheka site for about a month when an enforcement team raided the premises during Op Bersepadu Khazanah at 2.30pm.
The General Operations Force (GOF), together with the Pahang State Enforcement Unit (UPNP) and Lipis police, also seized seven vehicles, including five tipper lorries, an excavator and a wheel loader.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said, acting on information, the enforcement team went to the mining site and spotted six men clearing soil.
"The foreigners working at the site were told to produce their identification documents, but none of them had any.
"They also failed to produce any approval to carry out mining activities at the site.
"The foreigners were taken to the Lipis police headquarters, while the seized machinery and lorries were handed over to UPNP," he said.
Ahmad Radzi said investigations revealed that the six foreigners had been employed by a local man as labourers since 2024, and authorities were now tracking down their employer.
"They were brought to work at the illegal mining site about a month ago and worked for about 13 hours a day. They were paid RM10 an hour.
"They had been digging the soil and carrying out mining activities at the site without any authorisation from the local authority and the state government," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 426(1) of the National Land Code for unlawful extraction of rock material, which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
Ahmad Radzi said the six men were also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act for entering and remaining in the country without valid travel documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2 women injured as ambulance crashes into cars in Tumpat
Article:
KOTA BARU: Two women were injured when an ambulance believed to have suffered brake failure crashed into two cars at Simpang Tiga Kampung Neting, Jalan Kota Bharu-Pengkalan Kubor, Tumpat, yesterday.
Tumpat district police chief assistant commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said that in the 1.15pm incident, a Toyota Hiace ambulance, driven by a 43-year-old man from Kelaboran heading towards Pengkalan Kubor, experienced suspected brake failure upon reaching the location.
"The ambulance went out of control and collided with a Proton Waja driven by a 33-year-old woman and a Perodua Viva driven by a 29-year-old woman heading from Kota Baru.
"As a result of the collision, the driver of the Proton Waja suffered an injury to her head, while the Perodua Viva driver sustained injuries to her left knee," he said in a statement today.
He added that both victims were taken to Tumpat Hospital, while the ambulance driver was unhurt.
Khairi said a urine test conducted on the ambulance driver tested negative for drugs.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police advised all road users to ensure their vehicles were well-maintained to prevent untoward incidents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Binastra's Q2 earnings soar 78pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Binastra Corp Bhd's net profit rose 78.1 per cent to RM50.62 million in the second quarter ended July 31, 2025 from RM28.42 million a year ago, lifted by its construction segment.
Its revenue for the quarter climbed 65.9 per cent to RM658.39 million from RM396.84 million last year.
The construction segment was the group's primary revenue contributor, providing RM658.2 million versus RM396.6 million a year prior.
It also logged a higher pre-tax profit of RM70.6 million from RM36.3 million.
Binastra attributed the significant revenue increase to the group's newly acquired subsidiary, LF Lansen Sdn Bhd as well as its expansion into new construction services, particularly solar installation projects of RM97.4 million during the current quarter.
In comparison, revenue in the corresponding quarter last year was generated solely from conventional construction and data centre projects.
The company added that revenue from conventional construction and data centre projects during the quarter increased by RM164.2 million to RM560.8 million.
For the first six months of the financial year, the company's net profit rose to RM85.89 million from RM53.56 million while revenue came in higher at RM1.26 billion from RM653.68 million a year prior.
Binastra declared a first interim dividend of 4.0 sen per share for financial year 2027, amounting to RM43.8 million, payable on Oct 16.
"Our strong performance in the first half of FY27 reflects the continued progress of our core construction business and the benefits of our diversification strategy.
"We are particularly encouraged by the progress of our data centre construction activities.
"Since entering this segment, we have secured seven data centre projects with a combined value of approximately RM2.4 billion," said managing director Datuk Jackson Tan Kak Seng .
The company's outstanding order book has grown to about RM6.7 billion, providing Binastra with strong earnings visibility over the next four financial years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Mat Tok Gang' busted after nine break-ins
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: The 'Mat Tok Gang', which has been active in house break-ins in the Kuala Muda district since April, has been busted with the arrest of four men, including its leader.
Kuala Muda police chief assistant commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the suspects, aged between 28 and 40, were arrested during
Op Pintu/Op Lejang
on Sept 9 at several locations in the district, solving nine house break-in cases in Taman Delima and Taman Arked.
"The Mat Tok Gang is led by a 31-year-old man who operates with three accomplices, while two other suspects, known as Nizam and Jat Chai, are still at large," he said at a press conference at the Kuala Muda district police headquarters today.
He said the gang targeted unoccupied houses and stole valuables, including high-value vehicles such as motorcycles, while items seized included a drone, a motorcycle, a camera, a washing machine and three watches worth an estimated RM30,000.
Checks found that all four suspects had previous records for drug and criminal offences and tested positive for drugs, he said.
Hanyan said the suspects were being investigated under Sections 457 and 379A of the Penal Code for suspected involvement in house break-ins and motorcycle theft and had been remanded until Sunday.
"Further investigations are ongoing, including efforts to trace items they may have sold to other people," he said, urging victims who have yet to come forward to assist in the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Second body recovered in Pulau Ketam angler tragedy
Article:
KLANG: Another body, believed to be one of the anglers missing off One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam on Sunday, was found floating off Hutan Melintang, Perak, late this afternoon.
Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer, Maritime Lieutenant Mohd Syafiq Sazali said a local fishing boat spotted a man's body floating at 4.26pm.
"The discovery was immediately relayed to Perak MMEA for further action.
"The MMEA vessel KM Nusa, conducting search operations in the area, proceeded to the location about three nautical miles from the Selangor–Perak maritime boundary," he told reporters at the Search and Rescue (SAR) Forward Operating Base at the Sementa Jetty here today.
Mohd Syafiq added that the latest recovery was about two nautical miles from where the first victim, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, was found yesterday.

"The body, wearing a life jacket, will be brought ashore at the Hutan Melintang Jetty. Police will handle formal identification with family members or next of kin," he said.
Meanwhile, the family of missing angler Muhammad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, remains hopeful he will be found safe.
The victim's uncle, Khairul Muhidin, 47, said he last met his nephew, a contractor with a utility company, at his Jalan Kebun residence on Sept 4, where they mostly chatted about work.
"On the night of the incident (Sunday), I was shocked when family members informed me. I immediately dialled the 999 emergency line," he told reporters at the Sementa Jetty.
Khairul said the family is hopeful Muhammad Ridzuan is safe. He described his nephew, the fourth of six siblings and an avid angler, as resilient, noting he was wearing a life jacket during the incident.
"He might have held onto something or a container to stay afloat. Our main concern is dehydration at sea," he said.
Khairul said two other relatives who survived the incident, namely Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali and Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, both 45, are reported to be in stable condition.
"Mohd Rizal was transferred to a private hospital in Shah Alam, while Muhd Hamiszar, who suffered neck injuries, is being treated at Hospital Banting. Both are stable but remain traumatised by the ordeal," he said.
Earlier, Selangor Menteri Besar's Political secretary Saifuddin Shafi Muhammad, visited the victim's family and received a briefing on the latest developments of the incident.
Besides Mohd Rizal and Muhd Hamiszar, the other survivors were Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43, and boat skipper Zulfikalnain Awang, 47. The four were rescued on the second day of the SAR.
The two remaining missing victims are Muhammad Ridzuan and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamad, 49.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Affin Bank, IFC team up on US$400mil funding for MSMEs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Bank Bhd and International Finance Corp have jointly provided greater financing access for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with a US$400 million financing package.
The bank said the financing focuses on women-owned businesses and enterprises operating in underserved areas, aimed at broadening access to capital and strengthening support for MSMEs.
Under the agreed framework, Affin Bank will channel funding to eligible MSMEs to promote productive investment, enhance business competitiveness and contribute to more inclusive economic development.
Affin group president and chief executive officer Datuk Wan Razly Abdullah said together with IFC, the bank is expanding its ability to support businesses that have the potential to grow
"We believe greater access to capital is essential to advancing socio-economic development, strengthening local economies and creating opportunities for more Malaysians to participate in the nation's growth," he said in a statement.
IFC regional industry director Allen Forlemu said this partnership could create at least 42,000 jobs across Malaysia over the next five years.
This will improve access to finance for women entrepreneurs and enterprises operating outside major urban centers, especially the ones where the financing gaps are wider.
"We welcome working with a partner of Affin Bank's focus, experience, and expertise and appreciate their visionary leadership in supporting the growth of Malaysian MSMEs, including those owned by women, and uplifting underserved communities in places like Sarawak and Sabah," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police probe alleged road rage incident in Simpang Pulai
Article:
IPOH: Police are investigating an incident where a car driver was allegedly threatened with a wooden stick on Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai yesterday. The incident has now gone viral on the social media platform Threads.
District police chief assistant commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the incident occurred at 4.56pm when the victim, driving a Mercedes, claimed that his vehicle was forced to the side by a Toyota Vios before a misunderstanding arose after the victim honked at the other vehicle.
"One of the two men who got out of the Toyota Vios was accused of carrying and pointing a stick at the victim's brother. The incident was also recorded by a dashboard camera (dashcam)," he said.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code and efforts to track down the individuals involved are underway.
Therefore, he advised all road users to drive carefully, always control their emotions, and not act aggressively when facing any misunderstandings on the road.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Construction worker dies after falling from 20th floor in Penampang
Article:
PENAMPANG: A 20-year-old foreign construction worker died after he reportedly fell from the 20th floor of a building under construction in Jalan Bundusan here this morning.
The incident occurred at about 10.40am while the man was carrying out construction work on the floor before he fell.
Penampang district police chief Superintendent Sammy Newton said police received a report on the incident and a team was dispatched to the site.
He said officers from the Penampang district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division, together with the Sabah police contingent headquarters D10 Forensic Unit, inspected the scene.
"The victim's body was sent to the Forensic Medicine Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital I in Kota Kinabalu for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
"The case has been classified as sudden death pending the post-mortem results and further investigation," he said.
Those with information on the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Sergeant Major Patrick Duffy Francis Dicka at 013-8385335 or the Penampang district police headquarters at 088-712222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Electricity subsidy threshold expanded to households using up to 800kWh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has expanded the electricity subsidy threshold to domestic users consuming up to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month, up from 600kWh, from September until Dec 31.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was an immediate measure to ease the burden on households facing higher electricity bills.
This means that users consuming up to 800kWh a month will be exempted from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charges and Sales and Service Tax (SST).
Anwar said the higher threshold was necessary as hotter weather and haze had led some households to increase their electricity consumption, pushing their monthly usage above the previous 600kWh threshold.
"These conditions have driven higher electricity consumption among some households, causing their monthly usage to exceed 600kWh and resulting in unusually high electricity bills," he said in a statement today.
The measure was announced following a special meeting on immediate steps to ease the impact of rising electricity bills on affected households.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, had said yesterday that the meeting would involve the energy transition and water transformation ministry (Petra), Energy Commission (EC), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the finance ministry.
He said the government had taken note of public concerns over higher electricity bills in recent weeks and that the matter needed to be addressed promptly.
Anwar said the Madani government would continue to assess fuel costs and developments in the energy market to ensure electricity tariff decisions took into account household affordability, electricity supply security and the sustainability of the country's energy sector.
He also expressed appreciation to TNB, Petra and EC for helping to implement the measure.
Meanwhile, TNB had previously clarified that AFA did not, by itself, cause sudden increases in electricity bills, following concerns raised by some consumers.
In a statement,
the national utility company said
AFA was a two-way mechanism that adjusted electricity charges according to changes in fuel costs and foreign exchange rates.
When fuel costs fell, consumers received a rebate, while increases in fuel costs resulted in a surcharge.
TNB said the surcharge had been imposed since May following the crisis in the Middle East.
The AFA surcharge for September stood at 3.67 sen per kWh, it said.

Title: Malaysia offers Indonesia Bombardier aircraft, assets to tackle forest fires — Zahid
Article:
JAKARTA: Malaysia has officially offered assistance to Indonesia in tackling forest fires, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft previously deployed to help its neighbour combat similar fires.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the offer was conveyed to Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka during a meeting held in conjunction with his four-day working visit to the country, which began today.
Zahid, who is also the national disaster management committee chairman, said the assistance would also include three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
"The matter will be referred to President Prabowo Subianto for the Indonesian government's approval," he told a press conference after a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signing ceremony between the rural and regional development ministry and Indonesia's ministry of villages and development of disadvantaged regions.
The visit, which runs until Sept 20, is at the invitation of Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency (BPJPH) in conjunction with the fifth Halal 20 (H20) Summit.
Zahid is scheduled to attend the opening ceremony tomorrow and participate as a panellist in a session on regional halal cooperation.
The MMEA's Bombardier CL-415MP, which is capable of carrying out aerial firefighting operations, was previously deployed to South Sumatra in 2015, where it dropped 546,000 litres of water during a five-day mission.
Zahid said the aircraft would draw water from lakes, seas or rivers before dropping it over fire-affected areas, while the three helicopters offered would also be deployed for the same purpose.
"Malaysia is deeply concerned about this problem, which occurs every year, whether due to open burning in Kalimantan or Sumatra, with the resulting haze reaching Malaysia.
"We want to help Indonesia address the problem together," he said.
He said the assistance was not intended to interfere in Indonesia's affairs, but rather to help address transboundary haze, which also affects neighbouring countries.
"What is important to us is to resolve this problem before it happens. This means having a mitigation plan or a strategy to prevent it from happening. The mitigation plan is in the interests of both Malaysia and Indonesia," he said.

Title: Glomac swings back to black with RM7.6mil net profit in Q1
Article:

Its revenue for the quarter under review more than doubled to RM68.53 million from RM26.05 million in the same period last year.
The company said the increase was mainly due to higher contribution from the property development segment.

Article:

Title: Tasek Ipoh records country's highest API reading at 186
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 186 as of 6pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 32 areas recorded unhealthy API levels.
Seri Manjung, also in Perak, recorded the second-highest reading at 178, followed by Kuching and Serian in Sarawak, both at 173.
Samarahan in Sarawak recorded 168, while Johan Setia in Selangor recorded 165.
Other areas with high API readings included Nilai in Negri Sembilan (160), Putrajaya (159), Shah Alam (158), Pegoh Ipoh (157), Cheras (156), Banting (156) and Seremban (156).
Unhealthy air quality was recorded in Perak, Sarawak, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur, Kedah, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Penang and Terengganu.
Meanwhile, 33 stations recorded moderate air quality, with readings ranging from 51 to 100.
Sri Aman and Temerloh recorded the highest moderate reading at 100 each, followed by Larkin at 99 and Kuala Selangor at 98.
Only three stations recorded good air quality — Limbang in Sarawak at 49, Sandakan in Sabah at 40 and Kota Kinabalu at 39.
Under the API classification, readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.

Title: 'Not a sundry store': Aminuddin calls for firm stance amid crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has urged the state leadership to maintain a clear and firm stance, warning against changing positions during royal institutional crises.
He said the state leadership must avoid inconsistent positions that could lead to repeating past mistakes.
"To the leadership, do not repeat this. Changing positions constantly shows a lack of stance. One day it is this, the next day it is that.
"This is not running a sundry store; this is governing a state. There must be a firm stance," he said in a brief Threads post regarding the crisis in the state.
Aminuddin's remarks follow conflicting positions on the status of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan.
The Negri Sembilan government had earlier reported making a collective decision that the proclamation on the removal of Tuanku Muhriz was valid.
In a statement issued by the state executive council, the decision was said to have been made during a meeting chaired by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, with Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar recognised as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar with immediate effect.
The state government also noted that the state secretary was instructed to proceed with gazetting the proclamation according to existing regulations.
However, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undangan (DKU) Negri Sembilan maintained that Tuanku Muhriz remains the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan and that no vacancy exists as long as he lawfully holds the position.
Aminuddin also reminded leaders not to succumb to pressure or fear human opinions when fulfilling their duties.
"There is no need to yield to pressure; do not fear men. Fear Allah SWT in maintaining our honesty," he said, adding that he prayed for the state to remain peaceful, prosperous, and progressive.
The crisis deepened after Ismail stated on Sept 9 that he had signed a proclamation instrument under pressure and against his will.
Ismail stated at the time that the document failed to comply with processes under Article 10 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959, rendering it invalid and unenforceable.
Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on Aug 2, 2026, before Tuanku Muhriz following the state election, succeeding Aminuddin.
The DKU has since disputed the state executive council's actions regarding Tuanku Muhriz, stressing that the matter falls strictly under custom and the state constitution.
Aminuddin also noted that the state executive council lacks the authority to decide on the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959.

Title: Foreign worker compliance challenges
Article:
THE sight of 472 foreign nationals detained in Lebuh Pudu last week is more than just another enforcement headline.
It is a reminder that immigration compliance in Malaysia cannot be sustained by raids alone.
Enforcement may catch the problem but prevention is what keeps the system orderly.
And here, the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS) deserves more attention than it usually receives.
On Sept 13, the Mega Integrated Enforcement Operation checked 2,500 individuals in a single sweep.
Violations ranged from overstaying to using unrecognised documents.
The operation was triggered by public complaints about illegal premises and the visible presence of undocumented workers.
Yet the question remains. How do we stop these problems from piling up until they require mass detention?
FWCMS offers one answer. It is not glamorous and certainly not new, but it is a practical digital solution we have been building towards all along.
A Home Ministry parliamentary reply dated Feb 10, 2026 described FWCMS as supporting digital applications, approvals, monitoring and work-pass management.
It says the system brings together employer, quota, medical-screening and worker-entry information, while maintaining centralised records that can be audited.
The reply also identifies biometric verification as a safeguard against identity fraud, duplicate records and document misuse.
By digitising applications, biometric checks prevent duplicate identities. Dashboards flag expired permits.
Notifications can reach employers before lapses turn into violations. In short, FWCMS is designed to make compliance less about catching mistakes and more about avoiding them.
Consider the Bio-Medical Verification module. It ensures that the worker who undergoes medical screening is the same person who departs the source country and arrives in Malaysia.
That continuity matters when unreliable documentation is the biggest loophole.
For permit renewals, specifically for foreign domestic helpers, employers can now submit PLKS applications online up to 90 days before expiry, with ePASS replacing the old sticker system.
These are not flashy reforms, but they have proven to reduce red tape and give employers fewer excuses for negligence.
Making renewal processes accessible online gives the employers the chance to deal with documentation before deadlines loom, to prepare the necessary information, and to act responsibly rather than reactively.
In other words, digitisation does not just simplify paperwork, but it simplifies employer accountability.
FWCMS also has documented tools that can support more focused enforcement planning.
Its eEnforcement module is described as providing Immigration with preliminary information on expired work permits.
Separate notification and reporting functions allow stakeholder alerts through SMS, email or mobile applications, and reports are presented through dashboards.
These tools offer a way to turn administrative information into timely follow-up.
Nevertheless, the real measure of success lies in how these signals are used.
If records are outdated, alerts ignored, or officers slow to respond, the system becomes little more than a filing cabinet.
Accurate data and information only matter when they drive decisions and direct attention to cases that genuinely need scrutiny.
Employer accountability is the other half of the equation. Digital records must be kept with precise information to make compliance easier to track and harder to avoid.
A digital record gives businesses and agencies a clearer basis for reviewing an application's progress and the information submitted.
It also supports scrutiny of unresolved matters.
Departure administration has also been pulled into the digital fold.
Since September 2025, the Immigration Department notice states that Check Out Memo applications for PLKS holders must be submitted online through either MyPASS@JIM or FWCMS.
The notice states that manual applications at Immigration counters are no longer accepted.
This closes the loop as entry, stay and exit are now part of one connected compliance framework.
Workers themselves benefit when documentation is clear and accessible, allowing them to track applications, raise concerns, and avoid being trapped by administrative oversights.
However, effective implementation should include practical assistance for resolving record discrepancies and offering clear channels for reporting employment or recruitment problems.
The strongest case for FWCMS lies in its everyday impact through fewer expired permits, faster renewals, cleaner records and a system that is more transparent and can hold stakeholders accountable.
These are the small wins that add up to a more orderly labour market.
The Lebuh Pudu operation provides a clear reason to strengthen that preventive approach.
With accurate records, active employer participation and coordinated follow-up, FWCMS can form a key part of Malaysia's response to foreign worker compliance challenges, supporting effective enforcement and a more orderly system of lawful employment.
* The writer is a public policy professional with nearly a decade of experience across federal and state government agencies, as well as technology corporations. She is currently co-founder and creative analytics director of policy startup Wawasanex.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Couple's final breakfast before fatal motorcycle convoy crash [WATCH]
Article:
BESUT: A husband and wife who died in a road accident on Jalan Gong Kedak here this morning had stopped for breakfast with fellow members of their
motorcycle convoy
shortly before the crash.
Mohd Zamri Mohd Zaki, 41, and Norlyana Ismail, 45, were killed in the 9.45am accident.
Convoy participant Md Faizal Md Yusof, 52, said he had known the couple for only a month.
He said the group of 12 Aveta Nova 250 motorcycles left Kuala Terengganu at 7.30am and were heading to Kuala Perlis.
"Six motorcycles travelled with the couple while the other six riders travelled alone.
"We stopped for breakfast at an eatery near the accident site. After breakfast, we split into three groups and continued our journey," he said when met at the scene today.
Faizal said the first group, led by a marshal, departed first, followed by the second group, while he was in the final group.
"The couple were in the second group when the convoy collided with a lorry travelling in the opposite direction.
"I was only a few minutes behind them. When I passed the scene, I saw the victims lying by the roadside," he said.
He said although he had only recently met the couple, they were cheerful, enjoyed joking around and were enthusiastic about the three-day, two-night convoy.
"Following the accident, we decided to cancel the convoy, which had been planned for about a month," he said.
Meanwhile, Besut police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said Mohd Zamri and Norlyana, who were from Batu Rakit, were pronounced dead at the scene.
He said a husband and wife, aged 51 and 50 respectively, and another 51-year-old woman were injured in the accident.
"Initial investigations found that the accident involved a lorry driven by a 57-year-old man travelling from Jertih towards Bachok, Kelantan.
"The victims were riding three motorcycles from Kuala Besut towards Perlis," he said in a statement.
Rozaime said a motorcycle ridden by the 51-year-old woman was believed to have entered the lorry's path before the collision.
"The impact caused the lorry to veer off the road and collide with the motorcycle ridden by the victims, killing the couple at the scene.
"Meanwhile, another motorcycle ridden by the other couple collided with soil that had fallen onto the road," he said.
The bodies were taken to Besut Hospital for post-mortem.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Those with information can contact the investigating officer, Inspector Mohd Zulkifli Razak at 019-4475767 or the nearest police station.

Title: AGC: Exco statement has no legal effect, move to gazette or implement proclamation on N. Sembilan Yamtuan’s removal invalid, unconstitutional
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) said the Negeri Sembilan state executive council’s media statement or announcement has no legal effect as its members had no jurisdiction, authority or power under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 to make it.
The AGC said there was also no legal basis for the state executive council members to rely on the April 19, 2026 proclamation for their announcement, adding that any move to gazette or implement the proclamation would be invalid and unconstitutional.
In a statement today, the AGC said it had taken note of the document titled “Media Statement of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council — Decision of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council Meeting No. 6 of 2026 (September 15, 2026)”.
It said the Menteri Besar and state executive council did not have unilateral power to terminate or declare vacant the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, while the validity and effect of the proclamation must be determined through a valid constitutional and legal process, particularly under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
The AGC said it had previously given the preliminary view that the April 19 proclamation was invalid because it did not comply with the mandatory requirements under Article 10 of the state constitution, particularly as there was no evidence that any of the disqualifying factors under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
It said although the Datuk-Datuk Undang have the power to take action to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Article 10 also provides the procedures and grounds for consideration before such a decision can be made.
“To date, there are no facts indicating that the prescribed procedures have been complied with,” it said.
The AGC also said an issue had arisen over whether some of the Datuk-Datuk Undang who signed the proclamation were lawfully holding office, as they had been removed according to the customary practices of their respective luak.
“The validity of several Undang who signed the proclamation is disputed because their removal was carried out according to the customs of their respective luak,” it said.
“Therefore, the composition of the Undang Yang Empat was in fact incomplete at the material time,” it added.
The AGC said it respected the position of the Datuk-Datuk Undang and acknowledged that the appointment and removal of each of them were subject to the customary rules of their respective luak.
It said the 1959 state constitution also provides for the establishment of the Dewan Undangan dan Keadilan, with Article 16 placing matters concerning Malay customs, including the selection, appointment, placement and removal of Undang, as well as matters brought by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, under the Dewan’s jurisdiction.
Under Article 16(3), it said, the Dewan’s advice on such matters is final and cannot be challenged or questioned in any court on any grounds.
The AGC also said the matter was currently before the High Court of Malaya in Seremban and that an interlocutory injunction remained in force.
It urged all parties to respect the court process and allow the matter to be resolved in an orderly manner.

Title: Second body recovered as search continues for missing Pulau Ketam anglers
Article:
KLANG, Sept 17 — Another body, believed to be one of the anglers missing off One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam on Sunday, was found floating off Hutan Melintang, Perak, late this afternoon.
Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer, Maritime Lieutenant Mohd Syafiq Sazali said a local fishing boat spotted a man’s body floating at 4.26 pm.
“The discovery was immediately relayed to Perak MMEA for further action.
“The MMEA vessel KM Nusa, conducting search operations in the area, proceeded to the location about three nautical miles from the Selangor–Perak maritime boundary,” he told reporters at the Search and Rescue (SAR) Forward Operating Base at the Sementa Jetty here today.
Mohd Syafiq added that the latest recovery was about two nautical miles from where the first victim, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, was found yesterday.
“The body, wearing a life jacket, will be brought ashore at the Hutan Melintang Jetty. Police will handle formal identification with family members or next of kin,” he said.
Meanwhile, the family of missing angler Muhammad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, remains hopeful he will be found safe.
The victim’s uncle, Khairul Muhidin, 47, said he last met his nephew, a contractor with a utility company, at his Jalan Kebun residence on September 4, where they mostly chatted about work.
“On the night of the incident (Sunday), I was shocked when family members informed me. I immediately dialled the 999 emergency line,” he told reporters at the Sementa Jetty.
Khairul said the family is hopeful Muhammad Ridzuan is safe. He described his nephew, the fourth of six siblings and an avid angler, as resilient, noting he was wearing a life jacket during the incident.
“He might have held onto something or a container to stay afloat. Our main concern is dehydration at sea,” he said.
Khairul said two other relatives who survived the incident, namely Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali and Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, both 45, are reported to be in stable condition.
“Mohd Rizal was transferred to a private hospital in Shah Alam, while Muhd Hamiszar, who suffered neck injuries, is being treated at Hospital Banting. Both are stable but remain traumatised by the ordeal,” he said.
Earlier, Selangor Menteri Besar’s Political secretary Saifuddin Shafi Muhammad, visited the victim’s family and received a briefing on the latest developments of the incident.
Besides Mohd Rizal and Muhd Hamiszar, the other survivors were Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43, and boat skipper Zulfikalnain Awang, 47. The four were rescued on the second day of the SAR.
The two remaining missing victims are Muhammad Ridzuan and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamad, 49. — Bernama

Title: KL to add 49ha of green spaces as city moves to protect open areas, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will create nearly 49 hectares of new recreational spaces and public parks across the capital, as part of efforts to expand the city’s network of green areas and recreational facilities.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the strategic initiative included pre-development works and the utilisation of Department of Irrigation and Drainage reserves along Sungai Bunus and Kolam Ayer Panas.
She said the development will also cover the pond area next to Jalan Tasik Permaisuri 3, as well as a phased project at the Kampung Sungai Bohol Retention Pond.
“Our main aim under this initiative is not merely to create new recreational spaces, but to ensure that every valuable open and green space in Kuala Lumpur is legally gazetted and protected,” she said after inspecting the Bunus Flood Retention Pond here today.
She said the areas will be equipped with basic infrastructure suitable for people of all ages, particularly senior citizens and children, such as jogging tracks and lighting, while enforcement will be tightened to prevent encroachment or unauthorised commercial activities.
Hannah said that through the continued efforts of the Federal Territories Land and Mines Office (PPTGWP), 556 open-space lots have now been gazetted, while more than 200 others are in the final stages of the gazettement process.
She said the transparency of the gazettement process allows city residents to check the list of protected open spaces themselves through the MyHijau application on the official PPTGWP portal.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL allocates more than RM200 million under Budget 2027 for the green cluster, covering the management, preservation and upgrading of public facilities.
He said DBKL submitted an application to the Ministry of Finance under a matching grant scheme to upgrade 14 neighbourhood children’s playgrounds to safer, more modern designs. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian woman, 40, dies during scuba dive in Bali’s Crystal Bay
Article:
BALI, Sept 17 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman died while scuba diving in the waters off Crystal Bay, Desa Sakti, Bali, Indonesia, yesterday.
The victim, Siti Nuraini Rusidi, was reported to have died at about 11.10am local time, according to a report by
Sinar Harian
today.
According to local media portal BaliNews, Siti Nuraini joined a diving trip with a dive guide, boat captain and several other divers at about 8am.

The situation became tense after the group arrived at Crystal Bay, where they encountered very strong sea currents.
The conditions swept three divers away, while Siti Nuraini was reported to have died in the incident.
The incident later drew attention in Malaysia after a user shared details of the incident on Threads.

Title: Anwar: Malaysian households using up to 800kWh exempt from AFA, Retail Charge and SST on electricity bills until Dec 31 amid haze, heat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection for domestic users from 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to 800kWh a month from September to December 31, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post today.
He said the measure was an immediate step to ease the cost-of-living pressures faced by households, particularly as haze and hotter weather have driven up electricity consumption in some homes.

Title: Police probe Simpang Pulai road rage after Mercedes driver allegedly threatened with stick
Article:
